order: Restrict the review warmup to pinned checkouts and sync the docs. A warmup command writes — an engine import is not a read — so running it against a live tree means the review process modifying the user's working tree, exactly what a review must never do. The warmup exists because a fresh checkout lacks the generated artifacts a long-lived tree has, so pinned mode is also the only mode that needs it. Make a live-tree review say so in the preflight instead of silently writing, and name the flag that gets the warmup back. Cover it with two tests: the refusal is reported, and the file the warmup would have created does not appear in the project. IN SCOPE: the warmup's mode gate and its preflight line, those two tests, and the changelog, readme and field-validation wording. Constraint: leave the reviewer's tree-integrity check — its allowlist, its defaults and its reported wording — exactly as it is.
claims: A live-tree review no longer runs the warmup: the preflight states the refusal and names the flag that restores it, and the warmup runs only inside the throwaway pinned checkout. The changelog, both readme files and the field-validation notes were updated to match. Two new cases in the review-lane suite cover it — the refusal is reported, and the file the warmup would have created does not appear in the project afterwards. No other behaviour of the runner was touched.
